title: the-web-server-graduates-to-starlette
intention: Replace the stdlib http.server web_server with Starlette + uvicorn. The graft source is TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py — already built, already proven. The graduation brings async, WebSocket fan-out, and static file serving.
why: The trouble panel (and every future dynamic pane) needs client-side interaction and server push. The stdlib web_server is synchronous and cannot do either. This is not a new dependency decision — the framework was chosen in February and built in TheIgors.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass. The graft from TheIgors is bytes crossing from a sibling project; the graft ticket and proof are owed.
Law 4 — the framework was CHOSEN in February and confirmed by Akien; this is enforcement of that ruling, not a new decision.
one-web-server-surfaces-in-the-shim — ONE web server; a device gets a declared PANE, never its own route/port/server. This replaces, it does not add.

falsifier.proves_green: The stdlib http.server is replaced by Starlette + uvicorn. THREE things must hold: (1) existing pane URLs render identically — no regression on current surfaces; (2) WebSocket connection establishes and can receive a server push — the capability the current server lacks; (3) the listener is Starlette's ASGI app run by uvicorn, not custom socket code — the device logic (routing in server.py, rendering in render.py) stays where it is and does not leak into the transport.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) a second web server appears — the one-web-server rule is the standing constraint; (2) device logic (routing, rendering) leaks into the transport layer — server.py and render.py are the logic, Starlette is the transport; (3) existing pane URLs break — a regression is a red, not a tolerable transition cost; (4) the graft introduces dependencies not already in TheIgors' utility_closet_server.py without justification; (5) the graft enters without a graft ticket and proof (Law 8 — bytes are a graft with a ticket and proof, ideas are free and cited in the charter's entry).
falsifier.horizon: Before the-cairn-device-owns-the-trouble-panel — that ticket depends on this one for WebSocket capability. No blockers for this build; the graft source exists on disk and the framework is confirmed.

linked_ideas: Akien 2026-08-19: framework question on the trouble panel; Starlette confirmed as the ruled framework (CC's recommendation Feb 2026, Akien confirmed same session)

questions.a: This is a GRAFT from a sibling project, not a greenfield framework selection. The graft ticket and proof are owed (Law 8).
The shape (route -> fetch device DATA -> render) is already proven in the current web_server. What changes is the transport and the ability to push updates.
ONE web server — the rule holds. This replaces the current one, it does not add a second.
The listener (the socket binding) stays thin — Starlette's ASGI is the new listener, uvicorn is the runner. The device logic (routing, rendering) stays in server.py and render.py.

how: Replace stdlib http.server with Starlette + uvicorn. Graft source: TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py (already built + tested). One graft, one proof, one VALIDATION.

decisions.text: starlette 1.6.0 and uvicorn 0.52.4 are installed in the venv at $HOME/.cairn/venv (pip install starlette uvicorn; measured 2026-09-17 by python3 -c 'import starlette,uvicorn;print(starlette.__version__,uvicorn.__version__)'). httpx is NOT installed and is not needed: the proof drives the ASGI app in-process over raw scopes. No other package enters.
decisions.step: unlisted: Install starlette and uvicorn packages

decisions.text: The built cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py (commit bc8eb273) is the whole graft: module globals _device (a WebServerDevice, wired in main) and _bus; async handlers _handle_get(request) and _handle_post(request) that call _device.serve(path[, body]) and wrap the (status, content_type, body) it returns in a starlette Response — no rendering, no markup, no device logic in the transport; _handle_ws_troubles(websocket) accepts, asks the bus to='trouble' verb='live' and pushes the JSON list, removing the client from _ws_clients on disconnect; _make_app() returns Starlette(routes=[WebSocketRoute('/ws/troubles', ...), Route('/{path:path}', _handle_get, methods=['GET']), Route('/{path:path}', _handle_post, methods=['POST'])]); main(argv) keeps the prior listener's argparse (--port default 80, --bind default 0.0.0.0) and runs uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, host=bind, port=port, log_level='warning')).run(). From TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py only the wiring pattern is taken — Starlette app + Route/WebSocketRoute binding + uvicorn.Config/Server run — never its application logic; the docstring names the source file and this ticket.
decisions.step: unlisted: Replace listener.py with Starlette/uvicorn ASGI pattern from TheIgors

decisions.text: The standing proofs (test_web_server.py, test_web_server_chat.py, test_web_server_views.py, test_voyage_pane.py) exercise WebServerDevice.serve() without a socket and pass unchanged, because serve()'s contract is untouched. test_web_server.py additionally gained five teeth declared in PROVES for this ticket's five clauses (commit 6c233e3c): one web server in the tree; logic out of the transport; every pane URL byte-identical through the ASGI app driven in-process plus a WebSocket accept-and-push; no dependency beyond stdlib+starlette+uvicorn+cairn; the graft names its ticket and source. Green twice at HEAD, 4 of 5 red against the pre-graft listener.
decisions.step: unlisted: Verify existing proofs pass under the new listener

The graft source exists at /home/akien/dev/src/TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py (measured 2026-09-17: ls names it) and carries the wiring pattern named in D2 — a Starlette app with Route and WebSocketRoute bindings, run by uvicorn.Config + uvicorn.Server. Nothing beyond that pattern is taken.

The five teeth exist as built in commit 6c233e3c of cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_web_server.py, declared in its module-level PROVES = {'72e8e3509287': {'1': 'test_there_is_one_web_server', '2': 'test_device_logic_stays_out_of_the_transport', '3': 'test_existing_pane_urls_render_identically_through_the_asgi_app', '4': 'test_the_graft_brings_no_dependency_beyond_its_source', '5': 'test_the_graft_carries_its_ticket_and_proof'}}; each is a function in that file, and _main runs every tooth and prints PASS/FAIL per name. Nothing is left to implement.

The tester's command is python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli (cairn/devices/tester/cli.py, main at line 325) with flags --seal, --hollow <ticket>, --timeout <s>, -q; run with PYTHONPATH=. from the repo root. The validation it writes beside the proof is the tester's standard seal JSON: verdict ('green'|'red'), source_fingerprint, fingerprint_closure, isolation, and evidence.hollow[<ticket>] carrying the hollow reading — the same schema every validations/*.json in the repo already carries (cairn/devices/web_server/validations/test_web_server.json is the file it overwrites).

How main() obtains _bus and _device, as built (listener.py lines 103-116): _bus, heartbeat = connect_system(devices=['ground_loop', 'librarian', 'trouble']) — connect_system is the existing system-connection helper the pre-graft listener already used (imported at the top of listener.py), returning the bus and the heartbeat in one call; then _device = WebServerDevice(heartbeat, harbor_source=harbor_source(), port=args.port). No GroundLoop is instantiated and nothing is imported from ground_loop directly. The server then runs asyncio.run(uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, host=args.bind, port=args.port, log_level='warning')).serve()), printing one '[web_server] serving on http://<bind>:<port>' line first.

connect_system and harbor_source EXIST at cairn/tools/bus_client/bus_client.py (def connect_system(*, devices: list[str] | None = None, beat: bool = True) at line 132 returns (bus, loop) — the loop is the heartbeat the listener names; def harbor_source() at line 142 returns the harbor's traffic_image function). listener.py line 44 imports both: from cairn.tools.bus_client import connect_system, harbor_source. Nothing is defined for them in this ticket.

The startup pattern is asyncio.run(server.serve()) where server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, host=args.bind, port=args.port, log_level='warning')) — listener.py lines 117-127, as built. D2's earlier 'Server.run' wording is superseded by this line; .run() is not used. Handler details as built (listener.py lines 53-63): async def _handle_get(request: Request) -> Response: status, content_type, body = _device.serve(request.url.path); return Response(body, status_code=status, media_type=content_type). async def _handle_post(request: Request) -> Response: raw = (await request.body()).decode('utf-8', errors='replace'); status, content_type, body = _device.serve(request.url.path, method='POST', body=raw); return Response(body, status_code=status, media_type=content_type). The path is request.url.path (the catch-all Route '/{path:path}' is not consulted for the parameter); Request, Response, Starlette, Route, WebSocketRoute, WebSocket are imported from starlette.requests / starlette.responses / starlette.applications / starlette.routing / starlette.websockets.

The reference is the MODULE docstring of cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py (lines 1-5 as built): multi-line, and it names both '72e8e3509287' and 'utility_closet_server.py' as substrings anywhere within it — tooth 5 asserts substring presence on ast.get_docstring(module), so no particular line or format beyond 'both names appear in the module docstring' is required.
